subject: Production Impact: model variant flip causing latency & quality regressions — exec sync requested
messages:
From: Bryan Lim <bryan.lim@quantabank.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@quantabank.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: [QUICK] Post-upgrade latency/quality spike (prod)

Alex —

We started seeing increased tail latency and several generation quality regression reports shortly after the model stack update this morning (v2.1.3 -> v2.2.0 with qprofile=q4_1). Key observations: 
- P99 latency for our token-conditional generation endpoint jumped from ~420ms to ~1.5s between 08:12–08:45 PDT.
- Error rate (509/timeout) rose from 0.05% to ~1.4% during the same window.
- Business impact: ~3% of responses contained truncated or hallucinated account identifiers which is causing manual review backlog.

Attached is a small perf sample and application logs (perf summary). We rolled traffic to the previous model variant manually at 08:50 and saw p99 drop back toward baseline, but the surface area of bad outputs already caused some customer-facing failures.

Can you confirm whether the qprofile change was pushed by Redwood's automated rollout? We need an RCA and an ETA for a fix (or rollback) — compliance needs an official incident note.

Thanks,
Bryan
Engineering Lead — Platform
QuantaBank

- @marissa_cole: I'll need you to coordinate messaging to QuantaBank and capture the concrete customer impact for credits/SLAs.

I'll prepare an exec brief in ~30–45m. For now, can you confirm any customer-facing tickets opened on your side and approximate number of affected accounts?

Subject: Re: [QUICK] Post-upgrade latency/quality spike (prod)

Quick triage notes (initial):
- I pulled the qprofile trace (attached qprofile_trace_v2.txt). The v2.2.0 qprofile switched to int4-paths for several attention/tok-embed kernels but included a fallback path that is exercised for odd sequence lengths used by QuantaBank (their median seq=283). That fallback forces a slower GEMM kernel on the GPU which increases token compute and, apparently, raises p99.
- We also see that the new quantization path changes token sampling behavior at the decode step (subtle logits shifts) which can amplify hallucination likelihood on account ID fields for some prompt templates.
- The combination explains both latency and quality. The rollout should have been gated by our workload-specific compatibility check — preliminary guess: the workload fingerprint for QuantaBank wasn't present in the rollout's sample set.

Immediate recommendations:
1) Route QuantaBank to the previous stable model variant (v2.1.3 qprofile=q4_0).
2) Backfill a workload-specific qprofile test for sequence lengths 200–400 and regen the compat matrix.
3) Prepare a patch for the quant kernel to reduce fallback frequency; that will take a couple of days to validate.

Attachments: qprofile_trace_v2.txt (trace + kernel fallback markers).

I'll start a dedicated Jira (INF-4821) and paste a short technical RCA. If we need to accelerate a hotfix, I'm available to pair with infra.

—Grace
Applied ML — Redwood Inference

Routing/mitigation update: 
- I routed QuantaBank (account id QB-8742) back to stable variant v2.1.3 at 16:05 UTC. Confirmed via control-plane audit that traffic diverted and old variant instances warmed. Observed p99 trending back to baseline within ~6 minutes.
- Enabled prefix/KV cache warming for the session-heavy endpoints per Grace's note.
- Created fallback route_fallback_plan.md and attached here.

Short-term ask for execs: we'll need a scoped runbook to avoid automatic promotions to v2.2.0 until Grace's compatibility matrix is updated. Recommend a brief pause on the automated promotion for accounts with median seq > 200 until we validate the kernel behavior.

Log excerpts included in Jira INF-4821.

—Rishi

Subject: Exec brief: QuantaBank incident — model variant promotion caused latency & quality regression (summary + recommended remediation)

Team —

Summary (tl;dr): automated promotion of model variant v2.2.0 with new qprofile (int4-paths) caused kernel fallback on QuantaBank workload (median seq ~283) leading to p99 latency spikes and a small but material uptick in generation quality regressions (account ID hallucinations). We rolled QuantaBank back to v2.1.3 at 16:05 UTC which restored baseline metrics.

Impact: production P99 spike ~+1.0s for ~40 minutes; error/timeouts up ~1.3% during peak; several high-value transactions required manual review. Customer-facing impact requires credits and an incident note.

Root cause (short): rollout sampling missed QuantaBank's workload fingerprint; qprofile changes expose fallback kernel path for odd sequence lengths.

Recommended remediation (ops + commercial):
- Immediate: hold automated promotions for accounts with median seq >200; keep QuantaBank on stable v2.1.3 for 48h while we validate.
- Short-term engineering: implement compatibility test for sequence lengths and update rollout gating (ETA 2 business days).
- Medium-term engineering: patch quant kernel to reduce fallback window (ETA 5–7 days with QA).
- Commercial: offer QuantaBank a goodwill credit for the manual review overhead and waive one month of overage fees — ask finance for approval.

Requesting approvals: 
- Do we sign off on the proposed commercial package? (Finance Ops)
- Do we freeze the automated promotion for the affected cohort? (Product/CTO)

I'll draft the incident note for customers and send a proposed message for Marissa to use.

—Alex Martinez
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
